title: STILL PRESENT (r3): wrong-person awaiting UPDATE still unguarded — apply_wrong_person executes update_reference_call_status (status-only WHERE); the guarded mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person is called only by a direct-SQL test (vacuous pin)
evidence: form_handler.gleam: "case row.taken_over_at != "" { True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token) ... case row.correction_cycles >= 1 { True -> exhaust_wrong_person(...) False -> case sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated)" — update_reference_call_status.sql: "WHERE id = $1 AND status = $5::reference_call_status" (no taken_over_at clause); sql.gleam:1891 defines mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person but its only call sites are the test: "rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)" (1746, 1758). The route-driving test (1414-1442) takes over BEFORE the POST, so only the read-time gate is exercised.
detail: The executed awaiting UPDATE still has no taken_over_at backstop; the guarded SQL is wired nowhere but the direct-SQL test (the mandate's vacuous pin). Take-over keeps status contact_initiated, so a spoofed/redelivered wrong-person POST racing it still yanks the landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction and dead-ends it. Both mandate conditions unmet.
recommended_fix: Wire mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person into apply_wrong_person's awaiting branch (plus AND correction_cycles = 0, mirroring mark_awaiting_correction.sql), and add a POST-route test with take-over landing between lookup and UPDATE that turns red when the backstop is removed.

title: STILL PRESENT (r3): send_is_post_correction cast guard is start-anchored only — prefix-shaped malformed 'at' still raises and drops the delivery-failure event
evidence: CASE WHEN e->>'at' ~ '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}[T ][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}' THEN (e->>'at')::timestamptz >= rc.corrected_at ELSE false END
detail: Postgres ~ is a partial regex match; with only a ^ anchor, entries like '2026-02-31T00:00:00' or a date prefix plus trailing junk pass the guard and the ::timestamptz cast still raises, aborting the whole find query and dropping the webhook event — the failure the r3 N14sql fix claims to prevent.
recommended_fix: End-anchor the pattern (require $ plus optional Z/offset) or validate via a tolerant cast helper (e.g. CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE false with a savepoint-less try via regexp_replace), so any malformed entry stands the event down instead of raising.

title: wrong-person awaiting write path has no correction_cycles = 0 backstop — stale pre-correction POST can re-yank a corrected row into awaiting_correction and unlock a second correction (correction_cycles > 1)
evidence: mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql: "WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'contact_initiated'::reference_call_status AND taken_over_at IS NULL" (no cycles clause, unlike mark_awaiting_correction.sql:27 "AND correction_cycles = 0"); correct_reference_call.sql: "WHERE id = $1 AND application_id = $2 AND status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status" (no cycles cap)
detail: A stale wrong-person POST (read-time cycles=0) racing a correction + sweep T0 re-claim (status back to contact_initiated) re-yanks the corrected row (cycles=1) into awaiting_correction; the landlord's correct then succeeds again, bumping correction_cycles to 2 — the AD-7 one-cycle cap rests only on read-time gates on this leg.
recommended_fix: Add AND correction_cycles = 0 to mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql (matching mark_awaiting_correction.sql) and AND correction_cycles = 0 to correct_reference_call.sql as a hard SQL cap so a second correction 0-rows and 409s.
